specification.title: A migration whose reversal deletes its marker
steps: Runner A applies { m1 }. m1 inserts marker m1.
Revert with the framework's default selection. m1's reversal deletes marker m1.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the revert has returned and the reapply has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If a revert reports a migration as reverted, its history entry is absent and its marker is absent.

execution.description: Negative control. A COMMIT that does not raise is reported as committed, whatever cmd_status is. A COMMIT that raises is reported as rolled back. A failed savepoint rollback is ignored and the outer transaction is committed. A connection whose ROLLBACK failed is kept and handed to the next unit. A write made before a nested scope is sent inside that scope's savepoint. BEGIN ignores a requested isolation level.

configuration.write_before_nested_scope: deferred into the nested scope savepoint

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: A reported revert says the migration's effects are gone. The next apply is what shows that history and the database agree: the migration runs again.

api_outcome.basis: the unsafe control deleted the history entry and reported a revert
api_outcome.contract: The unsafe control takes no coordination lock. It reports a revert as reverted after deleting the history entry, and it does not delete the marker.
